Vance of Arden wrote this problem for a maths club. A ladder 522 metres long leans against a vertical wall. Its foot is 360 metres from the base of the wall, on level ground. How high up the wall does the top of the ladder reach, in metres? Answer with a whole number.

Yuri of Oakham wrote this problem for a maths club. A ladder 477 metres long leans against a vertical wall and its top reaches 252 metres up the wall. How far is its foot from the base of the wall, in metres, on level ground? Answer with a whole number.

Bea from Eastvale found this problem in a puzzle book. Ugo walks 16 metres due east and then 12 metres due north. How far is Ugo now from the starting point in a straight line, in metres? Answer with a whole number.

This problem comes from a quiz held in Norwick, set by Hugo. Will walks 510 metres due east and then 64 metres due north. How far is Will now from the starting point in a straight line, in metres? Answer with a whole number.
